description: Everyday conversation for golden-path steps 1 and 2 (meeting people at 18): greetings, asking after work, home, school, family and the news, the answers, raising a real subject, leaving, and the lie. Every part is a whole sentence American speakers said in federal transcripts (public domain: congressional hearings, the Congressional Record, NASA and U.S. House oral histories), counted also against the Library of Congress WPA life histories, 1936 to 1940. Record words are slots the game fills from the speaker's own records. Parts are grouped by the director's subject, role (ask, raise, reply, answer, lie) and choice; a group's parts are variants of one choice, never separate choices.

slots.name: A person's name from the records: someone both people know, or the listener's given name.
slots.employer: The speaker's employer, from their job record.
slots.claimed: The employer or town a lie claims instead, from a real record the speaker could name.
slots.my_employer: The player's own employer, from their job record.
slots.place: The town, as a resident says it, from the household record.
slots.my_place: The player's town, from their household record.
slots.school: A school, from the school record.
slots.years: A count of years, computed from two dated records.
slots.since: A month and year from a dated record, as people say it.
slots.my_since: The month and year the player started, from their job record.
slots.when: When the speaker last saw someone, from a contact record, as the director says it ("yesterday", "on March 3").
slots.my_when: When the player last saw that person, from a contact record, said the same way.
slots.relation: How the speaker is related to someone, with the possessive, from the family record.
slots.topic: What happened, from a news record the speaker heard.
slots.first: The given name of someone both people know, from the person's record.
slots.year: A year from a dated record.

mining.rule: A shape is kept when at least 2 documents say it as a whole sentence and one of them is a public-domain record from 2015 or later, which is its source.
